problem:
Which of the following matrices are block lower triangular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 5 & 9\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block lower triangular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A block lower triangular matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and the blocks above the main diagonal contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is a block lower triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- $B$ is a block lower triangular matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- $C$ is *not* a block lower triangular matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
\begin{aligned}C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ and $B$ only."
